title: org-admin-settings-wireframe-sprint-notes
summary: Working notes + early wireframe annotations for the Org / Team Settings surfaces. Focus: make RBAC discoverable, simplify API key lifecycle, standardize service account UX, and add practical audit log filters for SRE/security reviews. This doc is intentionally informal - collate thoughts from the sprint whiteboard and UX review on 2025-11-12.
goals: Clear separation of org-level vs team-level permissions
Fast primary task flows: create API key, create service account, assign role
Surface audit events that map to SLO-impacting actions (deploys, model swaps, key rotates)
Reduce support tickets around "lost key" and "who changed this policy?"
wireframe_notes: Landing: cards for Members, Roles & Policies, API Keys, Service Accounts, Audit Log. Quick CTA buttons on top-right: Invite, New Role, New API Key. Provide one-line status badges: number of seats used, keys expiring soon.
Members list: table with name, email, team(s), primary role, last active, badges for pending invites. Bulk action: change role, deactivate. Inline filter by role/team/email prefix.

Role editor modal: name, description, base permissions (checkbox grid grouped by surface: inference, billing, models, infra), attach policy rules (allow/deny), inheritance toggle (apply to sub-teams). Show example actions granted at top so non-experts understand impact.

API Keys page: two tabs - User Keys and Service Keys. Key cards show: name, owner, scopes, last used, created_at, expires_at, rotation schedule. Primary CTA: Rotate Key (creates new and marks old as deprecated). Danger flow: revoke with multi-step confirmation and recommended migration checklist.

Service Account creation flow: name -> associated team -> default roles -> key spec (one-time download OR KMS-wrapped key). Inline warning about single-download. Option to create short-lived credentials (recommended) with TTL slider.

Audit Log view: combined timeline with filters on actor, event type, resource (model, deployment, api-key, service-account), date range, and severity. Row expands to show before/after diff for policy changes. Save filter views for compliance reviewers.
Role/Policy comparison screen: two-column diff of policies (effective permissions) for quick audits before rollouts. Helpful for canary testing RBAC changes.
Mobile: simplified members list and audit timeline; no key creation on mobile (flagged in UI).
interaction_flows: Create API key (user): click New API Key -> name & scopes -> optional expiry -> preview allowed operations -> create -> show single downloadable token + copy button + link to migrate guide
Rotate Key (service): select key -> Rotate -> create overlay with migration window (default 48h) -> notify list of owners -> automatic fallback policy for 7 days -> old key marked deprecated
Create Service Account + Key: New Service Account -> assign roles -> choose key type -> generate -> download or wrap via KMS -> record owner and last-used metrics
Assign Role to Team: Roles page -> select role -> Assign -> choose target (team OR individual) -> choose propagation (immediate or staged rollout) -> schedule staging window for audit
Audit investigation: open audit log -> apply saved filter (deployments by user X last 30 days) -> expand event -> view resource diff -> link to implicated PR/CI run
Emergency revoke: from API Keys or Service Account -> Revoke -> require 2FA confirmation for owner if org-wide key; optional automatic reissue flow for Dedicated customers
open_questions: Should roles be editable in place or always fork-on-edit to preserve history? (Pros/cons listed in notes)
How to represent inherited permissions from org -> team without overwhelming UI? Consider hover-to-expand effective permissions.
Do we offer automatic key rotation for user keys or only service keys? Ops prefers automated for service keys only.
How to surface which deployments used a particular key without expensive tracing? Use best-effort last_used heuristics + linking from runtime traces.
KMS integration UX: show KMS key id inline? link to cloud console? minimum viable: boolean flag 'kms_wrapped' and external link.
Retention policy for audit logs in hosted vs dedicated vs private customers - default 90 days for hosted, configurable for enterprise.

acceptance_criteria: Role editor shows effective permissions for a target user/team before saving
API key creation returns a one-time token and records created_by, created_at, scopes
Service accounts can be created with either downloadable key or KMS-wrapped key
Audit log row expands to show payload diff and links to linked artifacts (PR/CI) when available
Saved audit filters persist per-user and can be shared to teams
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: users accidentally expose permanent keys -> Mitigation: default to short-lived keys, show strong warnings and provide rotate button
Risk: permissions complexity -> Mitigation: provide examples, sandbox preview, and role templates (billing-admin, deployer, viewer)
Risk: large audit log volume -> Mitigation: sampling for UI, offer export to S3 for heavy queries
